### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **1** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8259ea03e2959129c688639f69d0782c3a820f89` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fdb41f468559eb5c5ce4d0066ac934eaa5855025`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.page-template-closed-region-unplaced-refused.ts + packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts (checkPageRegionPlacement, PAGE_TEMPLATE_SLOTS, PAGE_TEMPLATE_OPEN_GRID, PageTemplateSchema, PageSchema.template default), packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts (page-template-full-width-to-default), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (the save door's verbatim branch and withDeclaredPageTypeDefault), packages/spec/scripts/build-upgrade-guide.ts (how reason is rendered), packages/spec/src/migrations/migrations.test.ts (the generic reason pins), and in objectui at 044f23193068 (the merge of objectstack-ai/objectui#12901) packages/components/src/renderers/layout/page.tsx and .changeset/12476-page-template-slots.md. The remainder of the diff, .changeset/24195-page-template-entry-reason.md, is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT and is judged here under ② only.

Inputs: card #24195, its body and all three comments (triage 6238135277, Claim 6238361195, os-dev report 6239553860); PR #24215, its body, its file list (2 files, +18/-2) and the net diff against main (merge-base a237d7f49); the check-runs on the head. The head had not moved at read time: refs/heads/claude/issue-24195-page-template-entry-reason is fdb41f468. Read at 2026-10-17T19:39Z.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies: none. The diff replaces the last sentence of one string literal, the `reason` of the semantic migration entry `page-template-closed-region-unplaced-refused`, and adds one changeset. `id`, `surface`, `replacement` and `acceptanceCriteria` are byte-identical to main; no Zod schema, export, conversion entry or registry template moves. `reason` is prose: `build-upgrade-guide.ts:136` prints it as the "Why not automatic:" list item, the only generic pin on it is `reason.length` above zero (`migrations.test.ts:139`), and the old wording occurs nowhere else under `packages/spec/src`, so no pin moves and none is owed. Judged right.

Each claim the new sentence makes, read in the cited code:

1. "served unchanged, and saving it again is refused until it is renamed" — carried over from the old sentence, still right. No path outside the spec calls `checkPageRegionPlacement`, `PAGE_TEMPLATE_SLOTS` or `PageTemplateSchema` (grep over `packages/**` minus spec: no hit); a stored row reaches the registry through `applyConversionsToStoredItem` (`packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts`, `packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts`), and the only conversion on `page.template` is `page-template-full-width-to-default` (`conversions/registry.ts:11444`), which rewrites `full-width` alone. The save door parses through `PageSchema`, which carries `PageTemplateSchema` at `template` (`page.zod.ts:1767`) and `superRefine(checkPageRegionPlacement)` (`:1974`), so the row is refused on save. Right.

2. "an unregistered template draws no layout, only a refusal naming the template and the registered templates" — objectui `page.tsx` at 044f23193068: `resolveTemplate` (`:599`) returns `UnregisteredTemplateRefusal` for any string `TEMPLATE_REGISTRY` lacks, and the dispatch (`:849`) renders that as the whole layout element, never reaching the `pageType` switch. Its text names `schema.template` and `TEMPLATE_NAMES`, every key of `PAGE_TEMPLATE_SLOTS` (`:302`, `:348`). Right.

3. "on a default, header-sidebar-main or three-column page an unplaced region is not drawn and moves into no other slot, and where it used to stack, under main, a refusal names it and the slots that template places" — `DefaultTemplate` passes `template="default"` into `RegionLayout`, where `extras` is empty and `unplaced` is the remainder (`:388`, `:389`), so nothing stacks; `HeaderSidebarMainTemplate` (`:494`, `:507`) and `ThreeColumnTemplate` (`:525`, `:541`) compute `unplaced` with `getRemainingRegions(regions, PAGE_TEMPLATE_SLOTS[template])` and hand it to `UnplacedRegionsRefusal` only, which sits directly after the `main` region in the main column in all three (`:437`, `:507`, `:541`). The refusal lists each region's name and `PAGE_TEMPLATE_SLOTS[template].join(', ')` (`:333` to `:341`). `dashboard` is correctly left out of the sentence: it is the open grid in the spec (`PAGE_TEMPLATE_OPEN_GRID`; `checkPageRegionPlacement` returns before the unplaced issue, `:1657`) and in the renderer (`DashboardTemplate` draws every other region as a cell), so a `dashboard` page has no unplaced region. A second region filling an already filled slot is not an "unplaced region" and is not covered by this sentence; the entry's earlier sentence ("was not drawn at all") still describes it, since `findRegion` takes the first of a name and `getRemainingRegions` excludes the name (`:90` to `:99`). Right. Minor: a `default` page whose regions name no slot at all (`!hasStructure`, `:391` to `:403`) draws the refusal alone, not under a `main`; "where it used to stack" still holds, and the text is not wrong.

4. "The exception is a page that names no template: it takes its page type's layout, which still stacks such a region under main" — `resolveTemplate` returns null for a falsy `template` (`:600`); the dispatch falls to `switch (pageType)` (`:855` to `:865`); each of `RecordPageLayout`, `HomePageLayout`, `AppPageLayout` and `UtilityPageLayout` calls `RegionLayout` with no `template`, where `extras` is the remainder and renders under `main` (`:388`, `:434` to `:436`). The spec still refuses that row's save: `checkPageRegionPlacement` reads `page.template ?? 'default'` (`:1629`). The exception is a stored-row-only case: a package page is parsed (`PageTemplateSchema.default('default')`, `:1767`), so it either carries `default` or is refused at `objectstack validate` and `build`; and the save door stores the authored body verbatim with `type` as the one grafted default (`withDeclaredPageTypeDefault`, `protocol.ts:2078`), so a template-less stored row stays template-less. objectui's own changeset says the same in its "Unchanged" paragraph. This sentence is the dev's one addition beyond the card's Expected; it is right, and without it the entry would claim a refusal a template-less row never draws.

5. Provenance: the sentence describes objectui at 044f23193068, the merge of objectstack-ai/objectui#12901, which is on objectui `main` (`merge-base --is-ancestor` exit 0), and whose `page.tsx` is unchanged on objectui `main` c83e3fe53 today (`git diff 044f23193068 origin/main -- page.tsx` is empty). Right as of this read; the pin is in ③.

6. Runtime-string rule: the new text names no tracker number; `ADR-0087.` is an ADR citation carried over. No backtick, pipe or angle bracket in the string; apostrophes only, escaped. The `⚠️` marker is kept in the position it had. Right.

Judged wrong: nothing.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/24195-page-template-entry-reason.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': patch`, `Clause-②: no`, no arm. It matches what the diff publishes: a text correction inside a released package (the entry's `reason` ships in the generated upgrade guide and in `os migrate meta` output), with no accept-set, export or conversion change, so `no` with no arm is the right declaration and `patch` is the right level; `skip-changeset` would be wrong because the package publishes the text, and `minor` is not owed because nothing widens. The PR body carries the same `Clause-②: no` line. No ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed (nothing breaks). The changeset body restates the new sentence consistently with the entry, template-less exception included, so the two texts do not diverge. `Check Changeset` on the head: success.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev declared `open_questions: []`. Its five deviations and two out-of-scope findings, each answered:

- D1, wording beyond the card's Expected (the template-less exception): answered in ①.4 — right and measured; the card's Expected alone would be wrong in the other direction.
- D2, one `origin/main` merge before the PR opened, main moved since: fine under Multi-agent §10; the merge commit carries no file change of its own (the net diff against main is the two files).
- D3, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` not measured locally: a declared narrowing; every `Lint ·` lane on this head completed success, so the gate's own verdict stands in CI.
- D4, gates 27 to 56 re-run after an overlapping build: a local-measurement note with no bearing on the contract; CI is the verdict.
- D5, commit trailers: e402d82e7 carries the AGENTS.md model-free pair; the merge commit carries none. Fine.
- OOS-1 (class b, release-text): three released copies of the old sentence remain — `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md:169`, `packages/objectql/CHANGELOG.md:128` and the consumed `.changeset/pre/23610-page-isdefault-template-slots.md:35` ("Stored metadata keeps loading."). Correctly not touched here: release-owned text takes a dedicated docs-only PR. ESCALATED to the seat: it needs a card or that docs-only PR, or the 18.0.0-next.3 CHANGELOG keeps saying "renders as before" beside a guide that says the opposite.
- OOS-2 (the template-less `pageType` path still stacks): the entry's last sentence now depends on objectui keeping that path; if objectui retires it, this entry needs a matching edit. Noted; nothing to do now.
- Transition window (PR body, "not handled here"): `.objectui-sha` is 5e15928b46, an ancestor of 044f23193068 by 38 commits, so the console this repository builds and serves today still stacks an unplaced region under `main` and still lays an unregistered template out by page type. The new sentence is ahead of the pinned console and describes the console the 18 guide is written for; the card's Expected and triage's grade both order that direction, and the pin bump is another card's single-claim path. ESCALATED to the seat: the pin bump to a commit that includes objectstack-ai/objectui#12901 (manifest regeneration included) must land before 18.0 GA, or the guide published at GA describes a refusal the shipped console does not draw. Until it lands, a `next` prerelease carrying this text is ahead of the shipped console by exactly this sentence — the window the card accepted when it asked for this wording.
- Governance: no governed surface in the file list, head repo equals base repo, 20 changed lines; no Tier H word is owed. `Governed Surface Queue Guard`: success.
- Check-runs on fdb41f468 at this read, 39 in all: 26 completed success — among them `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Build Core`, every `Lint ·` lane (ESLint, CI/release/engine gates, docs and code guards, repo and tooling gates, PM dispatch-gates, the two scoped lanes and the tooling self-tests), `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, the four claim and card guards, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Auto Label` and `filter`; 6 skipped by path filter or opt-in (`Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, the Dogfood Regression Gate matrix shards, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Packed-tarball smoke`, `Temporal Conformance`); 7 still in_progress — `Test Core (1/6)` to `(6/6)` and `Type Check · workspace`, which carry the required `Test Core` context and part of the required `TypeScript Type Check` context. None failed, none cancelled. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; this record does not pre-judge the ones still running, and the queue guard holds the landing until they are green.
